newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's 11-mo insurance premiums 13.6 bln reais.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's 11-mo insurance premiums 13.6 bln reais.

text.p: Brazilian insurance premiums in 1996's first 11 months rose 7.1 percent to 13.6 billion reais ($13 billion) over the same period in 1995, said state insurance watchdog Susep.
Susep said in a statement that car insurance accounted for 35.23 percent of all premiums, while health and life insurance accounted for 14.82 and 25.06 percent, respectively.
It said its premium figures differed from those provided by Brazil's National Federation of Insurance firms (Fenaseg) because Susep figures were not inflation-adjusted.
Earlier this week, Fenaseg reported Brazil's insurance premiums between January and November 1996 rose two percent to 14 billion reais over the same period 1995.
Susep said retained claims rose 20.29 percent between January and November to eight billion reais from 6.65 billion reais in the same period a year ago.

Technical provisions totalled 8.3 billion reais, of which 30.45 percent was invested in fixed-income assets, 17.14 percent in variable-income assets, 19.91 percent in real estate and 32.50 percent in public titles, Susep said.
